work.title: Étude in G♭ major, Op. 10 No. 5; Étude in G♭ major, Op. 25 No. 9
work.movement: Black Keys, followed by Butterfly — complete disc side

version.value: Two titles on one original disc side
version.note: The entire selected file is retained; the approximately 96.5-second junction is a listening marker, not a clip boundary. Individual score readings and cuts within each work have not been audited.

performers.note: Named on the selected source page.

date.note: DAHR master take 2; the other 1920 takes and later 1923 remake are not this selected master.

place.value: Camden, New Jersey, United States — Church Building
place.note: Place stated in the DAHR take table.

label.note: Victor is the issuing company in DAHR; the selected Archive item gives the Victrola imprint.

catalogue.note: Issue number of the 10-inch 78 rpm disc; this is not the matrix number.

matrixTakeSides.value: B-23953, take 2; both études on one side
matrixTakeSides.note: DAHR identifies Op. 10 No. 5 followed by Op. 25 No. 9; Archive’s matrix_number field repeats issue number 64989, so DAHR supplies the actual matrix.

credits.value: George Blood, L.P.; Chris Guest (transfer); Kevin Coupe (cleaning)
credits.note: Archive metadata names the scanning centre and the transferred/cleaned personnel; these are digital-transfer credits, not 1920 session engineers.

date.note: No transfer or mastering date is established; upload dates are not used as recording dates.

processing.value: 78 rpm transfer; flat and equalised versions documented, with 250 Hz turnover for the equalised versions
processing.note: Archive describes 3.5 mil truncated elliptical and 2.3 mil truncated conical styli. The selected generic MP3 is the provided listening derivative; the exact stylus/equalisation choice for that file is not established.

digital.format: MP3 listening derivative of a 78 rpm disc transfer

composition.note: Chopin died in 1849; this nineteenth-century composition is out of copyright in the programme jurisdictions. This does not determine the recording rights.

recording.value: Public domain in the United States: published in 1920
recording.note: DAHR’s issue record, MARC 264 field, dates Victor 64989’s publication to 1920 independently of the session date. The selected Archive item also gives 1920. This meets the programme’s published-on-or-before-1925 sound-recording rule; no non-commercial restriction appears in the Archive metadata.

rights.creditLine: Alfred Cortot, piano; Victor 64989, matrix B-23953 take 2 (1920). Transfer via George Blood, L.P. and the Internet Archive Great 78 Project; Chris Guest, transfer; Kevin Coupe, cleaning. Historical recording public domain in the United States.
